newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Layoffs set in Jamaica's sugar industry.
newsitem.headline: Layoffs set in Jamaica's sugar industry.

text.p: Nearly 17 percent of the 6,000 workers in Jamaica's sugar industry faced layoff Thursday following the government's announcement Wednesday that it would cut the workforce to improve efficiency.

Agriculture Minister Horace Clarke told workers yesterday at Frome, south of Montego Bay and the largest sugar factory in the Caribbean, that 978 workers would be laid off, 665 of them at Frome which employs 3500 people.

Frome and two other factories were sold to Sugar Company of Jamaica, a joint venture involving local rum distillers Wray & Nephew and the British firm Tate & Lyle three years ago. The government maintains a 24 percent equity stake in Sugar Co of Jamaica.

The company is producing sugar at a cost of US$0.21 a lb, while average world prices now stand at US$0.12 per lb, officials said. It has decided to mechanize its harvesting to bring down production costs.

Clarke laid part of the blame on the new owners. "If the restructuring had gone as it should then there should have been no need for layoffs as there would have been an increase in production and efficiency," he said.
